svg.text: The review's highest-leverage window — and the experiment nobody has run

g.title: TAG lipase (SDP1) tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context

Peroxisomal beta-oxidation tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: ros_leak_site rationale: Acyl-CoA oxidase is a flavoprotein that reduces O2 directly to H2O2 as part of its normal catalytic cycle — one of the few places in the cell where peroxide production is the intended chemistry rather than a leak. During germination that makes the peroxisome a major ROS source at exactly the stage the review argues matters most.
caveat: A flavin semiquinone is not well established in the acyl-CoA oxidase mechanism, and the enzyme's own catalase-rich compartment quenches the product quickly. Classed only as a ROS source, not as a radical-pair site.
Glyoxylate cycle (ICL, MLS) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT3G21720, AT5G03860
Acetyl-CoA tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N, 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G37510, AT5G08530, AT4G02580, AT5G11770 rationale: The FMN site forms a flavin semiquinone during turnover and is a known superoxide-producing leak site, and the Fe/S chain performs sequential one-electron transfers — both of the physical routes the radical-pair and hyperfine arguments require. No published experiment has applied a near-null field and measured plant complex I activity, so this is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.
caveat: Electron transfer along the Fe/S chain is fast relative to plausible singlet-triplet mixing times, so a coherent radical-pair effect here is harder to argue than at the flavin. Treat the flavin and the cluster chain as separate hypotheses rather than one.

Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_copper_binuclear, cu_a_binuclear, heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H rationale: The review names cytochrome oxidase explicitly as a candidate direct metabolic target. The heme a3/CuB centre passes through paramagnetic oxygen intermediates (P, F, oxoferryl) whose spin states are, in principle, field-addressable.
caveat: Strongly exchange-coupled metal centres relax very fast, which argues against coherent spin effects. This is a mechanistically attractive but physically demanding hypothesis, and is labelled T3 for that reason.

Aconitase (ACO1/2/3) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT4G35830, AT4G26970, AT2G05710 rationale: The review nominates aconitase as the sentinel of Fe/S integrity, and the biochemistry supports it: the exposed cluster iron makes aconitase the first TCA activity to fall under oxidative stress, so it reports cluster damage before anything else does.
caveat: Precisely because aconitase responds to any oxidative insult, a change under NNMF would NOT by itself implicate a magnetic mechanism. It is a sensitive readout and a poor discriminator; it needs a paired ROS-independent control.

ATP / ADP ratio (pre-photosynthetic) tier T4 (reported) quantum class: structural_context Nietzel2020: Mitochondrial energy metabolism is redox-kick-started during seed germination, establishing that respiratory competence is restored before photosynthesis. [10.1073/pnas.1910501117] Rosental2014: Primary metabolism is activated and regulated during seed germination, with respiration supplying the energy for reserve mobilisation and cell expansion. [10.1017/S0960258513000391]

Mitochondrial superoxide / H2O2 tier T2 (reported) quantum class: ros_leak_site AGI: AT3G10920 Parmagnani2022: Near-null magnetic field exposure alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis. [10.3390/biom12121824] Farooq2021: Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, establishing the route from mitochondrial ROS to a developmental outcome. [10.3389/fpls.2021.781734] rationale: Not a magnetosensitive mechanism itself — it is the amplifier. A field effect too small to measure as a rate change can still register here, because ROS signalling is threshold-like.

Cytochrome c tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H AGI: AT1G22840, AT4G10040 Racca2022: Cytochrome c and the transcription factor ABI4 link mitochondrial status to ABA-dependent seed germination. [10.1111/nph.18287] rationale: A one-electron heme carrier, paramagnetic in the ferric state. Included because Racca et al. place cytochrome c on the path from mitochondrial state to germination timing, which is the developmental window the review argues matters most.

Radicle emergence tier T4 (reported) quantum class: structural_context Farooq2021: Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, defining the window in which a respiratory lesion would have most leverage. [10.3389/fpls.2021.781734] Eckardt2005: Peroxisomal citrate synthase provides the exit route from fatty acid metabolism in oilseeds, linking reserve mobilisation to the TCA cycle. [10.1105/tpc.105.034843]

svg.text: Before chloroplasts mature, an oilseed embryo is entirely heterotrophic: stored triacylglycerol must be mobilised, run
through peroxisomal beta-oxidation and the glyoxylate cycle, and converted to ATP by mitochondrial respiration. That
makes the first 0-72 hours after imbibition the window where a respiratory or Fe/S lesion would have most leverage, and the
reason Arabidopsis and Brassica are comparable systems for the review's argument. The original Figure 6 carried a
summary table of "normalized trend ranges" for germination rate, radicle length, ATP status and seedling vigour; those
were qualitative cross-study impressions rather than measured values, so no number from them is reproduced here. The
map shows the route and the endpoints; any quantity has to arrive from projected data. Every node on this map is T3 or T4,
which is the honest state of the field: the review's central proposal is a geomagnetic-versus-near-null imbibition time
course, and no such experiment exists in its bibliography. Derived from: Figure 6 of Porterfield & Barker, "Plant Responses to
Near-Null Magnetic Fields" — expanded to the reserve-mobilisation route and bound to Arabidopsis loci. Node counts by
evidence tier: T2=1, T3=5, T4=5. Schematic topology only — no quantitative value is encoded in this base map; numbers
appear only when measured data is projected onto it.
